snapshot_decision.judgment: ACCEPTABLE for the B2 check; not an export-byte custody guarantee
snapshot_decision.reason: The check retains an observation and digests, not bytes for subsequent consumption. A no-follow regular-file read whose device/inode/size/mtime/ctime are unchanged before and after, whose consumed size matches the initial stat, and whose full digest matches the declaration is appropriate historical measurement evidence on the host local filesystem. The previous reproduced mixed-generation read now refuses. Retaining a private copy at check time is unnecessary when no later consumer is entitled to reuse those bytes or infer their continuing presence from PASS.
snapshot_decision.boundary: B4 must independently open and materialize verified private snapshots, rehash against the selected exact candidate/master digests, and build exclusively from those snapshots. A historical/replayed B2 PASS cannot authorize changed bytes, substitute for B4 custody, or prove present-day currentness. Matching stat metadata is a normal local-filesystem mutation check, not a cryptographic filesystem generation counter or protection against a privileged host fabricating stat results.
snapshot_decision.documentation_note: Section 5 line 293 still says re-hash from verified private snapshots while lines 298-303 explicitly choose generation-checked reads without check snapshots. Update that leftover introductory phrase to match the accepted boundary.

M2.verified: FIFO/nonregular rejection remains. High-level read requests now use remaining_limit+1, and an over-limit stream returns a nonmatching sentinel. wait_for maps the caller timeout to OperationalEnvelopeExceededError before the observation/stage transaction, and the new PG test asserts zero observation rows for its sleeping measurement. That test was source-read; the user reports 22 PG passes, not reviewer execution.
M2.remaining: wait_for cancels the coroutine/Future awaiting asyncio.to_thread, not an already running executor thread. The synchronous _assets/_measure worker has no cancellation signal, per-chunk deadline or process boundary; after the caller gets the typed error, it can continue reading and measuring further assets. Per-role byte ceilings bound consumption only if reads make progress; they do not bound the wall time of a stalled regular-file read. Repeated timed-out calls can leave default-executor workers occupied and affect unrelated to_thread users. This is the retained bounded-worker/cancellation portion of M2, not a new duplicate finding. The new PG sleep test proves caller timeout and no receipt, not worker termination. N3 separately qualifies the strict raw byte-budget claim.
M2.evidence: A minimal fresh wait_for(to_thread(worker),0.05) probe printed worker started=True and worker finished=False at timeout; the worker completed only after an explicit test release. Event-loop executor-shutdown cleanup subsequently timed out in this restricted environment, so this is bounded observed semantics, not a completed service/PG test. The full-service stub probe produced no completed output and was interrupted; no product claim relies on it.
M2.fix: Finish the already requested worker-cancellation boundary: use a managed worker whose lifetime can be bounded, or establish and enforce a narrow supported local-I/O contract plus cancellation checks that stop further assets/chunks and account for live timed-out workers in a bounded dedicated executor. A byte limit alone must not be described as a wall-time bound. Persist a test that observes worker exit/no further work after caller timeout; a sleeping function that eventually returns does not prove this.

L.title: Buffered fdopen still fetches beyond the claimed limit-plus-one raw read budget
L.status: CONFIRMED with actual raw descriptor position
L.scenario: os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb") creates a buffered reader. For a 3 MiB file and limit=1000, _measure calls handle.read(1001), but the buffered reader has advanced the underlying raw descriptor to 4096 bytes before returning the oversized sentinel. The new Spy records only calls to BufferedReader.read, so sum(requested)<=1001 passes while the raw read budget is exceeded. This does not permit oversized data to PASS integrity and has bounded buffer-sized impact; it invalidates the exact fetch-budget claim and its regression evidence.
L.fix: If limit+1 is the actual descriptor-read budget, use unbuffered reads or bounded os.read and assert the raw bytes fetched. If the intended budget is only bytes returned to the hashing loop, state that explicitly in the design/docstrings/tests instead of claiming no additional bytes are fetched.
